U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services

Non-Precedent Decision of the Administrative Appeals Office

In Re: 27665130

Date: MAY 21, 2025

Appeal of California Service Center Decision

Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker (Extraordinary Ability)

The Petitioner, a machine learning researcher, seeks classification as an individual of
extraordinary ability in the sciences. See Immigration and Nationality Act (the Act)
section 203(b)(1)(A), 8 U.S.C. § 1153(b)(1)(A).

The Director of the California Service Center denied the petition, concluding that the
record did not establish that the Petitioner meets at least three of the ten initial
evidentiary criteria at 8 C.F.R. § 204.5(h)(3)(i)-(x). The matter is now before us on
appeal. Upon de novo review, we will remand the matter for further proceedings.

I. ANALYSIS

The Petitioner claims eligibility based on criteria relating to participation as a judge of
the work of others, authorship of scholarly articles, and a high salary in relation to
others in the field.

The Director concluded that the Petitioner satisfied the criteria relating to judging under
8 C.F.R. § 204.5(h)(3)(iv) and scholarly articles under 8 C.F.R. § 204.5(h)(3)(vi), and we
agree with those conclusions.

Evidence that the beneficiary has commanded a high salary or other significantly high
remuneration for services, in relation to others in the field. 8 C.F.R. § 204.5(h)(3)(ix).

The Director determined that the Petitioner's compensation evidence was insufficient without
addressing the comparative wage data the Petitioner placed in the record. The decision does
not reflect consideration of this material evidence. Because the Director's decision did not
adequately address the evidence relating to this criterion, and because a finding in the
Petitioner's favor would bear on whether a final merits determination is required, we will
withdraw the Director's decision and remand the matter.

On remand, the Director should evaluate the comparative salary evidence, determine whether
the Petitioner satisfies at least three criteria, and if so, conduct a final merits
determination considering the totality of the record.

II. CONCLUSION

ORDER: The Director's decision is withdrawn. The matter is remanded for the entry of a new
decision consistent with the foregoing analysis.
